points.description: States that a prototype program simulates (or models/replicates) the behaviour of software. Accept equivalent wording such as 'shows how the software will behave' or 'imitates the behaviour of the system'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer identifies a prototype as an early/sample version or model but does not say that it simulates behaviour.

levels.says: Identifies the prototype as an early/sample version or model of the software, but does not state that it simulates behaviour.

points.description: Specifies that the simulation covers portions or parts of the software, rather than necessarily the whole system. Accept 'parts of the software', 'some of the software's behaviour', or equivalent.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer refers to simulating software or a system but does not make clear that only portions/parts are simulated.

levels.says: Refers to simulating software or a system but does not make clear that only portions/parts are simulated.

points.description: Specifies that the portions belong to the desired software product, i.e. the product to be built, not an existing or finished system. Accept 'the software being developed', 'the intended product', or equivalent.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer refers to a software product but does not make clear that it is the desired/to-be-built product.

levels.says: Refers to a software product but does not make clear that it is the desired/to-be-built product.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the answer to say that a prototype program simulates behaviour and that this simulation is of portions of the desired software product. Part marks are available for identifying the prototype as an early/sample model, for mentioning software simulation without limiting it to portions, or for referring to a software product without saying it is the desired product. No marks are earned for answers that do not mention simulation or modelling of software behaviour.
